Vijayawada: YSRCP president
YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the Chandrababu Naidu-led coalition govt of neglecting farmers affected by Cyclone Arnab, alleging that the administration was exaggerating its preparedness while failing to assess crop losses and provide relief on the ground.
Addressing a video conference with party district presidents from cyclone-affected areas on Thursday, Jagan questioned the govt’s claim that crop damage was being assessed through CCTV footage monitored at the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS). He alleged that officials were announcing changing estimates without conducting a comprehensive field-level assessment.
Jagan claimed that preliminary information indicated severe crop damage across nearly 12 lakh acres. He said paddy crops in Konaseema, East and West Godavari and Anakapalli districts had suffered extensive damage. Coconut, banana and aquaculture farms were also affected. He alleged that power disruptions had damaged aquaculture operations by affecting aerators.
According to Jagan, farmers were facing losses of around Rs 40,000 per acre in paddy, Rs 2 lakh per acre in banana and up to Rs 45 lakh per acre in aquaculture.
He accused the govt of understating the extent of the damage and failing to provide adequate assistance to affected farmers.
He also criticised the govt over pending input subsidies for losses caused by Cyclone Montha last year, claiming that nearly Rs 600 crore remained unpaid. He alleged that the withdrawal of free crop insurance, the weakening of Rythu Bharosa Kendras and the failure to provide zero-interest crop loans had increased farmers’ vulnerability. Jagan further alleged that the coalition govt had failed to fulfil its investment assistance commitments under Annadata Sukhibhava. He said farmers had been promised Rs 60,000 over three years but had received only Rs 19,000, leaving Rs 41,000 pending.
He said farmers, who had already faced drought conditions, were now struggling with cyclone-related losses. He appealed the party leaders and workers to support affected communities. Jagan asked them to visit villages, interact directly with farmers and residents, and extend assistance wherever possible. He specifically urged party cadres to ensure that procurement agencies purchased rain-soaked and discoloured paddy rather than leaving farmers to bear the losses.
He alleged that relief operations and restoration of essential services remained inadequate despite the govt’s claims of preparedness. Jagan asked party leaders to coordinate efforts across affected districts and provide reassurance to farmers and residents. Senior party leaders, regional coordinators and district presidents participated in the video conference.
